content.comment_body: Hello, I have a home network with [article_no] master and [article_no] slave modules that work well together. Now, I want to add a [article_no] module for controlling my heating system. My question is: Can the [article_no] master communicate with another [product_name] [article_no] master, for example to switch an output on the other module? Thank you, [user_name]

To do this, you need to set up a data link between the [article_no] devices. Start by creating a network project and add the new module, the [article_no], along with the master and slave modules. The Ethernet connection will be created automatically; you just need to set the correct IP addresses. If you want, I can prepare a sample project for you.
Do you have a sample setup for this scenario? Thank you.
Could you clarify what kind of example you need? Are you looking for all possible connection configurations?

I want to set up [product_name] version 8 as the master and [product_name] version 7 as the slave, covering all possible connection scenarios. I also want to use this setup on the web server tool ([url]). Thanks.

Is there a specific reason you aim to use a master/slave configuration? A master/master connection is generally more advantageous. In master/slave, only the master runs a program while the slave device only provides hardware resources. With master/master, each device can have its own program.
My goal is to control outputs on [product_name] version 7 from [product_name] version 8. For example, I want an input on version 8 to trigger an output on version 7. Thank you.
Here’s a video demonstrating how to set up a network project with [product_name] version 8 as master and [product_name] version 7 as slave.

You mentioned master/master configuration is preferable. In that case, can you connect inputs and outputs between different modules in master/master? The example you provided seems fine, but I’m curious why you recommend master/master over master/slave. Is it necessary to define version 8 as master in the configuration?

One issue with configuring both [article_no] modules as masters is that [article_no] devices can't send network outputs directly to a master module. This works only between a master and a slave. However, there's a workaround so you can control outputs of version 8 master from version 7 master.

Here's an example showing how to establish communication between a [article_no] master and a [article_no] master. Using user-defined functions for 'LowByte' and 'HighByte', you can send up to 15 digital signals from version 7 to version 8 over a word using the VM-area.

When I try to set up a master/master connection, I don't see the version 7 device listed as expected. My interface appears different from what's shown in your video example (see attachment). I'm also using [product_name] Control in my setup.
Please refer to the video in the attachment for guidance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking to integrate different versions of [product_name] modules into a home automation network, aiming for bidirectional control of outputs between devices. They are unsure about setting up master/slave and master/master network configurations due to restrictions in certain versions on network output control. There is confusion regarding the configuration steps, and users are requesting examples and clarification on best practices, particularly for connecting different generations of modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward communication and control between [product_name] modules of different versions, including the ability to trigger outputs across versions and configurations. They look for clear instructions and example projects to guide them through the setup process.
